title: A Pass Not in the Ledger

goal.text: Climb the Cairnstep and see if it belongs on the map.

steps.label: Climb the cairns to the notch
Compare the old and new drawings

plate.narration: Stacked stone cairns climb a narrow notch between snowy peaks. Wind combs the ridges. Far above, griffin aeries cling to the cliffs like nests on a shelf.

cairns.narration: Stone cairns climb a slope toward a notch in the Frostfang Peaks. By the lowest one sits a griffin keeper called Brask, from the aerie on the cliffs. He has a heavy pass ledger open on a rock and a pencil behind his ear. "This path was not in my ledger last season," he says. "Real pass, or trick of the snow? Tonight, climb the Cairnstep with me, and help me decide if it belongs on the map."

steps.narration: The cairns climb in steps of old snow over loose stone. Brask flaps ahead. "Touch every cairn as you pass," he calls. "It is polite, and it helps you balance." How will you climb?

climb_line.prompt: Everyone climb the cairn stairs together, one hand on the stones.
climb_line.narration: One cairn is so neat you want to give it a medal.

onSuccess.narration: Cairn by cairn, you reach the top. Not one stone falls.

onFailure.narration: A cairn topples and bounces away. You finish with scraped hands.

climb_scout.prompt: The surest feet pick a way up the loose slope.
climb_scout.narration: The surest feet go first. Everyone else follows, like ducklings.

onSuccess.narration: The route holds. You reach the notch without a slip.

onFailure.narration: The first route ends at a drop. You take the long way and arrive tired.

climb_leap.prompt: Use leap to bound over the loose stretch with a rope.
climb_leap.narration: Your manticore crouches, rope in its teeth.

onSuccess.narration: One bound, and the rope is tied. You climb it like a staircase.

onFailure.narration: You land short, but the rope reaches. You climb on wobbly knees.

climb_rally.prompt: Use rally to keep tired legs climbing.
climb_rally.narration: Your songkeeper starts a bouncy song, with a new beat for every cairn.

onSuccess.narration: Legs that wanted to stop remember how to go.

onFailure.narration: The song is cheerful, but the slope is steep. You reach the top puffing.

notch.narration: At the notch, the wind combs your ears. Far off, a distant island floats in the sky, small as a loaf in a pond. Brask waves a flag on a stick, and a tiny flag answers. "Our neighbors," he says. "They watch the weather. We watch the stones."

ledger.narration: Brask opens his ledger. Last season's drawing shows a smooth ridge. This season's shows the notch you stand in. A pencil line marks the herders' grazing route, cut by floodwater in three places. "One drawing is wrong," says Brask. "Which?"

ridge.narration: You hold the old page up against the real mountain. The cairns line up. The ridge does not. A slab of stone has stepped sideways, like someone in a crowded room. "Find me exactly where it moved," says Brask.

ridge_spot.narration: There! A step in the rock, where the drawing says smooth. Brask makes a neat pencil mark.

supplies.narration: You lay the herders' route over the new drawing. The new path runs above the three flooded spots, along a high, dry shelf. "So the herd could use it," says Brask, "if the shelf is real. Where does it meet the cairns?"

supplies_trace.narration: Your finger lands on the spot, right where the ridge has a new step in it. Brask taps it with a claw. "Yes. There."

ledger_sky.narration: Your flyer goes up for a look. From above, the two drawings fit together like halves of a cracker, and the step in the ridge is as plain as a nose.

compared.narration: The pages agree on all but one thing: a step in the ridge, where stone slid sideways after the first snow. "The drawing was right," says Brask. "The mountain changed." He taps the page. "Next, the cairns. Do mine stand in the order the new page shows?"

cairn_order.narration: Brask points at three cairns. One leans. One has a flat top. One has two stones side by side, like shoes. He hands out paper scraps. "Clues. Read them out loud."

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then put the cairns in the order of the drawing.
clues: The leaning cairn is at the start of the line.
The twin-stone cairn is at the end.
The flat-topped cairn stands between the other two.

onSuccess.narration: Lean, flat, twin! "They agree," says Brask.

onFailure.narration: Brask swaps two back. "Cairns are patient," he says.

onAssisted.narration: You lay the scraps side by side, and the order falls out.

pebble.narration: A young griffin skids up the slope, hugging a rolled page. Her beak is inky. "This is Pebble," says Brask. "My apprentice. She draws the new page each season." Pebble's feathers droop. "I drew the ridge in the first snow, and it was whole! Did I draw it wrong? Will you help me fix the page?"

pebble_help.narration: Pebble holds out her page. It has a smudge where a tear fell, and a flap that keeps blowing up. She scraped her wing on the climb, too. How will you help?

pebble_walk.prompt: Lead Pebble along the narrow ledge to the step without a slip.
pebble_walk.narration: Pebble keeps stopping to look at her feet.

onSuccess.narration: She sees the step and gasps. "It is not my mistake. It is the mountain's!" She draws it in at once.

onFailure.narration: Pebble wobbles, and you catch her. She sees the step from there and draws it in.

pebble_page.narration: The wind keeps grabbing the page. You pin it down with a stone on each corner. The wind sulks and gives up. Pebble draws the step in three quick strokes.

pebble_mend.narration: Your unicorn strokes Pebble's wing once, softly. The scrape fades. "It stopped hurting!" she says, and draws the step in three quick strokes.

pebble_done.narration: Pebble blows the ink dry. The new page shows the notch, the step, and a tiny signature: Pebble. "It was true when I drew it," she says. "Now it is true again." She hugs you and gives you a squashed supper bundle. "Nervous packing."

drawing_memory.narration: Pebble taps the marks of her page on a rock. Griffins learn a drawing by heart this way. "Watch twice, then tap it back."

interaction.cue: Watch Pebble's pattern, then tap it back.

onSuccess.narration: Pebble beams. "Now the page lives in all our heads."

onFailure.narration: One tap lands wrong. Pebble repeats it slowly until it sticks.

onAssisted.narration: Pebble taps slowly, and you tap along until you have it.

moved.narration: Now the big question: will it hold? The slab that moved is as big as a barn. "Test it," says Brask. "Gently. It has been through enough." How will you test it?

test_roll.prompt: Roll a stone along the slab and listen for a hollow place.
test_roll.narration: Solid rock sounds one way. Hollow rock sounds another.

onSuccess.narration: Rattle, rattle, rattle, steady all the way. Solid rock.

onFailure.narration: The stone rolls into the snow. You hear one hollow thump, somewhere.

test_lean.prompt: Everyone lean on the slab together and see if it shifts.
test_lean.narration: Everyone leans, as if pushing over a very patient cow.

onSuccess.narration: The slab does not budge a hair.

onFailure.narration: The slab grumbles and shivers. Everyone leaps back. Then it is quiet.

test_brace.prompt: Use brace to push on the slab while the others look for cracks.
test_brace.narration: Your thornguard plants both feet and pushes.

onSuccess.narration: The slab does not budge, and no crack opens.

onFailure.narration: The slab shivers, then settles. Steady enough, but you hold your breath.

test_smash.prompt: Use smash to shove the slab.
test_smash.narration: Your bigfoot leans on the slab with both hands.

onSuccess.narration: A mighty shove, and the slab shrugs it off.

onFailure.narration: The slab shivers. A little grit trickles, then it settles.

tested.narration: The slab is steady, settled like a cat on a cushion. But at its edge, a little stone drops through a gap and falls a long way. "The neck," says Brask quietly. "The narrow bridge of rock at the top of the pass. It is hollow underneath."

survey.narration: Brask pulls out a long knotted cord. "Now we measure. Length, width, and any spot that would make a goat say no." A long shelf of snow runs along the cliff. Where will you start?

survey_shelf.narration: Everyone takes a stretch of cord and walks it out along the shelf. It hums in the wind like a harp. Brask counts the knots and nods.

survey_pace.narration: At each cairn, you pace from cliff to edge, counting out loud. Pebble counts in griffin, which has different numbers. Still, your counts agree.

survey_sky.narration: Your flyer swoops along the pass. From above, it is a long white ribbon with a pinch in it.

survey_done.narration: "Four hundred steps long," Brask writes. "Two goats wide. One hollow neck." Pebble adds a tiny goat for scale. Brask gives you six coins from the aerie's purse and an owlfeather clasp. "Fee and badge," he says.

rest_tea.narration: Brask lights a tiny stove that hisses like a cat. His tea tastes of pine needles and warm stones. Everyone gets a mug. Pebble gets a thimble. The neck can wait a minute.

tea_share.narration: Brask gets the cheese, Pebble the bread, and the wind the crumbs. Pebble gives you a lace from her satchel. "It makes feet quick." Far below, tiny dots move along the valley. "Herders," says Brask. "They will want to know if this path is real."

tea_x.narration: The tea is terrible and wonderful. Far below, tiny dots move along the valley. "Herders, with their goats," says Pebble. "They will want to know if this path is real." Brask nods. "Then let us finish."

pages_x.narration: The old pages smell of dust and pencil. Some passes are crossed out. A few have a tiny star. "Every road in this book was new once," says Brask. He taps the blank page. "Someone has to walk it first. Today, that is you."

shelter.narration: Brask taps the ledger. "If herders come this way, where can their grain sacks wait out the weather?" Along the shelf, the cliff leans out in overhangs, and snow piles deep. Where will you look?

shelter_drip.prompt: Read the overhangs and find the driest one.
shelter_drip.narration: Drips mean wet. Dust means dry.

onSuccess.narration: You find a deep, dry nook out of the wind.

onFailure.narration: The first nook drips on your head. The second will do.

shelter_dig.prompt: Dig a snow hollow deep enough to hide a stack of sacks.
shelter_dig.narration: Snow makes a fine roof if you dig it right.

onSuccess.narration: The hollow is deep, with a roof as smooth as an egg.

onFailure.narration: The roof drops a cold lump down your neck. You prop it with a stick.

shelter_leap.prompt: Use leap to reach the high overhang.
shelter_leap.narration: No goat could climb to that ledge. Your manticore crouches.

onSuccess.narration: One bound, and you are up. The ledge is dry and sack-shaped.

onFailure.narration: You land short and scrabble up. Still, the ledge is dry.

shelter_cover.prompt: Stretch the waxed cover over a nook and pin it against the wind.
shelter_cover.narration: Brask sells you a waxed cover that smells of candles.

onSuccess.narration: The cover snaps tight like a drum.

onFailure.narration: The wind flaps a corner. You pin it with rocks, and it holds.

shelter_found.narration: Pebble draws a tiny roof on the map. Then a yip floats over the rocks. A cinder wolf, gray as ash and glowing at the edges, is nosing at the little cairn where the aerie keeps its hay and bread. A second wolf trots up. "Hungry, not wicked," says Brask. "But that is my winter hay."

cache_fight.narration: The wolves creep toward the cairn, tails glowing. They are hungry, but not very big. A good shout and a firm stand should do it.

onVictory.narration: The wolves bolt in two puffs of ash. In their paw prints, Brask finds a warm bead and gives it to you.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves dart off with a loaf and some hay. "Hay can be bought," says Brask. "Friends are harder."

neck.narration: The neck is a narrow bridge of rock. Below it is a gap you could drop a house into. "Travelers will cross here," says Brask. "They need to know how." How will you check it?

neck_rope.prompt: Cross the neck on the rope, one at a time, keeping to the middle.
neck_rope.narration: You tie the rope to the last cairn. Below, the gap yawns.

onSuccess.narration: You cross and come back safely. The neck holds, if you keep to the middle.

onFailure.narration: A stone slips under a foot and falls for a very long time. The rope holds.

neck_tap.prompt: Tap along the neck with a staff and find the solid rock.
neck_tap.narration: Solid rock says tock. Hollow rock says donk.

onSuccess.narration: You find a solid strip in the middle, exactly one goat wide.

onFailure.narration: The taps all sound alike to you. Brask shows you the safe line.

neck_done.narration: The safe way runs down the middle, one traveler wide. Brask draws it as a dotted line. "A goat could walk it," he says. "A goat should walk it on a rope. Now, what do we write?"

mark.narration: Brask holds his pencil over a clean page. "There are three ways to write it, and each is true. A ledger is a promise to the next traveler." Pebble holds her breath. What goes on the page?

mark_open.narration: Brask writes OPEN in big letters. "The herd will be glad," he says, a little too quickly. Pebble clears her throat. "And the neck?" Brask looks at it a long moment. "Let us at least put up a good cairn."

mark_warn.narration: Brask writes OPEN, WITH CARE, and draws a tiny hat on the neck. That is how griffins mark a place that needs respect. "Travelers read warnings," he says. "Mostly." Pebble copies the hat. "And a tall cairn to go with it."

mark_closed.narration: Brask writes UNSETTLED in small letters. "The ridge moved once. I will not send a herd over a thing that might move twice." It is a careful answer, and a bit sad. "We will still raise a cairn," he says. "A closed road deserves a good marker."

capstone.narration: The last cairn goes up at the neck. "One set of hands holds, one set lifts," says Brask. He counts to three, then four, because he counted wrong.

interaction.cue: Hold the cairn steady while your friend lifts the capstone.

onSuccess.narration: The capstone settles with a click.

onFailure.narration: It lands crooked. Brask taps it straight with his pencil.

onAssisted.narration: You wedge the cairn, and the capstone slides on.

capstone_done.narration: The wind whistles politely around the new cairn. Pebble holds up a small stone. "This goes on top. You do it." She also gives you a brass whistle. "For a moment that needs one loud note."

variants.text: Brask ties a tiny hat-shaped warning flag to it.
Brask ties a white ribbon to it, to say the road is resting.

last_stone.narration: Brask has scratched a mark in the middle of the capstone. The wind keeps nudging your hand.

interaction.cue: Tap when the stone is over the middle scratch.

onSuccess.narration: Click! Right in the middle. Brask tips his head, deeply moved.

onFailure.narration: The stone rolls off. Pebble sets it on top herself. "Practice," she says kindly.

signal.narration: Brask lifts his flag toward the distant island. "Our neighbors will want to hear what we found," he says. "What shall we tell them?"

signal_wave.narration: Brask hands you a flag. Big wave, little wave, circle, pause. It is like a dance with a very strict teacher. Across the sky, a tiny figure waves back. "Oh, nicely done," whispers Brask.

signal_whistle.narration: You point Pebble's whistle at the island and blow. The note flies across the sky like a thrown spoon. A tiny figure on the island jumps, then waves.

signal_back.narration: The island's flags answer. "They say thank you," Brask reads. "And the ridge is not the only thing that moved. Their old landing route now points into empty sky. I would like to know how."

variants.text: The island's flags answer. "They say yes," Brask reads. "Their old landing route now points into empty sky. I would like to know how."

message.narration: Brask ties the ledger shut. "We know where the ridge moved, and what travelers should do," he says. He looks at the island flags. "Our neighbors have route trouble too. We griffins can fly you over to them, if you like."

variants.text: Your open-pass notice sends the herders toward the new crossing, with Pebble's sketch of the neck beside it.
Your warning stays with the notice. Brask will lead the herd across in small groups, with a watcher at the neck.
Brask hangs your closed-pass notice. The herd will keep its longer route until the new ridge weathers a storm.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
